steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Functionalism (Durkheim, Parsons): society is a system of interdependent parts working together to maintain stability. Each institution has a function: family socialises children, education teaches skills, economy provides material needs. Society is based on value consensus (shared norms and values).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Marxism (Marx, Engels): society is divided by class conflict between the bourgeoisie (owners of production) and proletariat (workers). The ruling class controls the economy and ideology (institutions like education and media maintain ruling class dominance). Capitalism exploits workers and creates false consciousness (workers accept a system that exploits them).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Feminism (Oakley, Barrett): society is patriarchal (male-dominated). Liberal feminism seeks reform through legislation. Marxist feminism sees patriarchy and capitalism as intertwined. Radical feminism sees patriarchy as the primary form of oppression, present in all institutions. Difference feminism recognises different women experience oppression differently.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Interactionism (Becker, Goffman): society is created through everyday social interactions and meanings. Labelling theory: people are labelled and act according to those labels (Becker: 'deviance is not a quality of the act but of the response of others'). Goffman's dramaturgical model: social life is like a performance on a stage.

steps.body: Compare Functionalism and Marxism as sociological perspectives. | Explain how Feminism challenges traditional sociological perspectives. | Evaluate whether Interactionism provides a more valid view of society than Functionalism.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Functionalism = CONSENSUS (society works together). Marxism = CONFLICT (society is exploitative). Marxism: bourgeoisie vs proletariat, false consciousness, ideological control. Feminism: patriarchy, gender inequality across institutions. Interactionism = micro (individual interactions). Functionalism/Marxism = macro (social structures). Both levels are needed.
